page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.4xlarge is an arm64 memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by 16 dedicated physical cores based on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 microarchitecture running at 2.8 GHz, with a single execution thread per core. The cache hierarchy provides 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory totals 128 GB, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The server includes an integrated 950 GB NVMe SSD for fast local instance storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate exceptional memory subsystem throughput. In synthetic memory testing, the instance registers in the top ten percent, achieving uncached large-block read bandwidth of 296.76 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 130.55 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is robust, with Geekbench multi-core scores and PassMark database operation benchmarks placing in the top quartile. Single-threaded metrics, including Clang compilation and stress-ng tests, align with median baseline values. Machine learning inference benchmarks reveal lower efficiency during text generation, reflecting the lack of discrete GPU hardware or matrix acceleration.

In terms of qualitative efficiency, the custom ARM Neoverse-V2 design delivers high memory density and steady multi-core execution per resource unit compared to traditional x86 alternatives. Bundling 950 GB of local NVMe storage reduces reliance on remote network-attached disks for high-IOPS scratch space. Amazon Web Services r8gd.4xlarge is well aligned with memory-intensive workloads, including high-throughput in-memory caching systems, distributed data processing, relational database management systems, and intensive ETL pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gd.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by 16 dedicated physical cores of ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 128 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per core ratio, alongside a bundled 950 GB NVMe SSD instance storage volume and 8 Gbps baseline network throughput. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier memory performance, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 296.76 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 130.55 GB/sec. Multi-core compute performance and database transaction throughput place in the upper quartile. While single-thread CPU benchmarks deliver median results and large-language model token generation exhibits low throughput, the hardware exhibits strong density for memory-bound data tasks. The r8gd.4xlarge is engineered for memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caches such as Redis, real-time analytics, and low-latency storage-backed enterprise pipelines.
